linked_issues.title: Support needs to refund part of an order

source.description:
Support can only refund an order in full, through the console. MER-1988 asks for partial refunds, and finance wants them auditable.

This adds POST /orders/{order_id}/refunds, backed by a new RefundPolicy that caps the cumulative refunded amount at the order total and the number of refunds at orders.max_refunds_per_order (10). Orders grow a refunded_cents column and a partially_refunded status; migration 0044 backfills it from the refunds table.

The console keeps working: omitting amount_cents refunds the remaining balance.

coverage.note: Every hunk was read, including the regenerated client.

story.headline: Refunds become partial and cumulative, and move from the support console to the API.

beats.label: Was
beats.text: A refund was all-or-nothing, gated on the order's `refunded` status.

beats.label: Now
beats.text: `RefundPolicy` answers how much is still refundable, against a running total.

beats.label: Watch
beats.text: It ships as `POST /orders/{id}/refunds`, alongside two unrelated changes.

tests.note: `test_policy.py` pins the cumulative maths; `test_refunds_api.py` drives the endpoint.

intent_delta.stated: Add a partial-refund endpoint backed by a cumulative policy, with a migration that adds refunded_cents and a partially_refunded status.

also_does.summary: Changes `money.to_cents` from truncation to ROUND_HALF_UP, which alters the minor-unit amount for any fractional input.
Lowers `api.max_page_size` from 200 to 100 in the same config hunk that adds the refund limit.
Drops the `fully_refunded` column and removes it from `OrderResponse`, which the description implies but does not state.

change_map.summary: One new rule, one new endpoint, a column replacing a boolean, and the ripple through schemas, client and docs.

checks.title: 0044 drops orders.fully_refunded while backfilling refunded_cents

checks.title: The Stripe refund is created before the policy check runs
checks.why: `create_refund` calls `gateway.refund`, then `record_refund`, which is where `policy.check` raises. A 409 leaves a refund at Stripe with no ledger row.

checks.why: The refund reaches Stripe in `create_refund` before `policy.check` runs inside `record_refund`.

checks.title: OrderResponse drops fully_refunded and adds refunded_cents

checks.title: docs/api/refunds.md replaces the once-only refund rule

rule.quote: An order may be refunded more than once.
rule.was: An order can be refunded once. A second attempt raises `RefundError`.

checks.why: The documented rule every caller of the refund path was written against is replaced in this change.
checks.question: Which callers still expect a second refund to raise `RefundError`?

checks.title: Concurrent refunds on one order serialise on a row lock
checks.why: The running total is read under `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, held for the rest of the transaction, which makes no network calls. Different orders do not queue.
checks.question: Does serialising per order hold up at your peak refund rate?

checks.title: Orders gain a partially_refunded status
checks.why: The migration writes it to existing rows and the ledger writes it going forward. Anything matching on `status == 'paid'` or `'refunded'` sees a new value.
checks.question: Where do you match on order status exhaustively?

checks.title: New write endpoint behind the refunds:write scope
checks.why: `POST /orders/{id}/refunds` is the first route gated on `refunds:write`. Whichever tokens already carry that scope can now move money through the API.
checks.question: Which tokens already carry the `refunds:write` scope?

checks.title: api.max_page_size drops from 200 to 100
checks.why: Unrelated to refunds, and in the same hunk as the refund limit. It takes effect at the next boot and halves the largest page any list endpoint returns.
checks.question: Does any client page through orders assuming a 200-item page?
